scenes.title: The well
text: The village well. The rope's new, which is more than you can say for anything else here.

extra.text: Ida said not the well: folk need it. Stream water, from up the hill.

choices.label: Drink and fill your waterskin
choices.result: The well water tastes of stone. You drink your fill and top up the skin.

extra.text: "Bite first. Bess is down by the gate. Go on."
Ida looks up from the arrow she's fletching. "Bess has seen to you? Good. You'll live, then."
"Deadwood and that boar. Rook knows where. Go on, the pair of you."
"Look after him. And yourself." She doesn't look up from the arrow, but her hands have gone still.
Ida doesn't quite look at you. There's a bow hung over the lodge door that wasn't there before.

choices.label: "Thank you, for the road."
choices.result: "Don't. I was after that wolf anyway." She frowns. "You were lucky I was."

choices.label: "What happened to Skelmed?"
choices.result: "The levy happened. Half of every catch to the crown, and the collector takes his own bite on top. The young ones went inland. The merchants stopped coming when the roads went bad." She spits. "And now wolves on the coast road. Wolves, with eyes like that. In my grandmother's day you'd never see one this side of the hills."

choices.label: "We're back. Rook isn't."
choices.result: Ida doesn't say anything for a long time. "He was nineteen," she says at last. She goes into the lodge and comes back with his old jerkin and boots, and a dagger, and puts them in your arms. "Take them. He'd want them used." Then, quieter: "Things are getting worse around here. If we don't get help soon, this village is done for. He was going to go to Eastmere for us." She looks at you. "Somebody still has to."

extra.text: "Bed, bread or bandages? I've all three, and potions for the bad days."
"Saw what you did at the net shed. Most anyone's done for this village in a year. What can I get you?"
Beds are thirty coppers. Sleeping saves your game.

choices.label: Rent a bed for the night (30 coppers)
choices.needText: A bed's 30 coppers, and you haven't got them.

choices.label: Buy a loaf of bread (6 coppers)
choices.needText: You haven't six coppers to your name.
choices.result: Bess wraps a loaf in a cloth. "Yesterday's. Still good."

choices.label: Buy a bandage (15 coppers)
choices.result: Bess fetches a roll of clean linen from a chest. "For the cuts. There's always cuts."

choices.label: Buy a flask of spirits (30 coppers)
choices.result: "Don't drink it all at once. Or at all, really. It's for wounds."

choices.label: Buy willow bark (10 coppers)
choices.result: "For fevers. Brew it, it's foul. Or there's a willow up by the hill stream, if you'd rather pick your own."

choices.label: Buy a health potion (40 coppers)
choices.result: "Old Maud up the coast brews them. Tastes like rust, works like a charm. Keep one back for the bad days."

choices.label: Buy a sewing kit (80 coppers)
choices.result: "Needle and good thread. Stitched up my husband with that, twice."

scenes.speaker: Dockhand
scenes.title: A dockhand
text: "Crabs come up on the sand south of the pier. Mind the claws, but the meat's worth it, if you've a knife."

scenes.speaker: Bess
scenes.title: You're bleeding
text: A broad woman in an apron is haggling with a carter over a basket of fish, just inside the gate. She takes one look at the blood on you and forgets the fish.

"You'll be Ida's stray. She ran past shouting about a wolf." She's back in a moment with a flask, a roll of linen and two little red bottles. "Sit down before you fall down. Bites go bad if you leave them. Clean it first, then bind it. Spirits for the cleaning, mind, not for drinking."
"The red ones are health potions. Drink one when you're badly hurt, or give one to a friend. They heal, they don't raise the dead, so don't wait too long. I sell them, when you've the coin."
"Go on, you do it. You'll be doing it yourself on the road, with no one to help."

choices.label: Take the things, and see to the bite

extra.text: "You'll be Ida's stray. Sit down before you fall down."
"Go on, I'm watching. Clean it first, then bind it. Your pack, the Survival page (S). I'm not going back up that hill till it's done."

scenes.title: Ida
scenes.speaker: Ida
script: say:Ida:"There's a dozen of us left in Skelmed and most of them are old. The woodshed's near empty, and we've eaten nothing but fish for a month."
say:Ida:"Take our guest up the hill. Deadwood for the shed, and that boar that's been rooting up the garden. Bring back both."
say:Rook:"Wolf-bitten and straight out hunting." He grins at you. "Ma likes you. Come on, the forest's up the north lane."

scenes.title: Ida
scenes.speaker: Ida
script: say:Ida:"Well. Look at that." She walks round the boar twice. "Clean kill. And the shed'll be full by dark."
say:Ida:"You came out of the sea with nothing, and the first thing you did was help us. That's rarer than you'd think, round here."
say:Ida:She hands you an armful of leather and a dagger in a worn sheath. "Rook's old jerkin and boots. He's grown out of them, he just won't say so."
say:Ida:"And a proper blade. That fish knife won't stop anything bigger than a crab."
say:Rook:"I've not grown out of them." A pause. "...They pinch."
narrate:Ida's smile goes. She looks past you both, down the street, at the boarded doors.
say:Ida:"Rook. Things are getting worse around here. If we don't get help soon, this village is done for."
say:Ida:"Wolves on the coast road with eyes like that. The levy. Half the houses empty. We can't mend that with bows."
say:Ida:"I want you to go to Eastmere. Find the reeve, the guard captain, anyone who'll listen, and tell them what's happening here."
say:Rook:"Eastmere? That's days on a bad road."
say:Ida:"Then you'd best not go alone." She looks at you.
say:Ida:"You can look after yourself. I've seen it. Go with him and see him there safe. There's nothing for you here but fish."
say:Rook:"Ready when you are. I'll be at the north gate."

scenes.title: The north gate
script: say:Rook:"Eastmere's inland, east past the forest and over the hills. A few days, if the road's kind."
narrate:And so you leave Skelmed behind you, with Rook at your side and the road to Eastmere ahead.
narrate:This is where the opening ends for now. Eastmere, and the road to it, are being built next.

scenes.title: The north gate
script: narrate:And so you leave Skelmed behind you, alone, with the road to Eastmere ahead and Rook's dagger at your belt.
narrate:This is where the opening ends for now. Eastmere, and the road to it, are being built next.
